item.title: Marvel’s Wolverine has kicked off no end of debates on social media, with the latest of these centering around a chase sequence that sees Logan weaving through traffic on a motorcycle.
item.description:
Marvel’s Wolverine has kicked off no end of debates on social media, with the latest of these centering around a chase sequence that sees Logan weaving through traffic on a motorcycle.
Insomniac’s new superhero game is the latest hot-button topic in the gaming community. Well before it even released, players were calling out early gameplay footage shown off by the media, taking umbrage with a Sentinel boss fight (it was too formulaic), its voice acting (who hired these anime voice actors for my grisly X-Men game?) and Logan following a scent trail to track down enemies (too hand-holdy).
Now that it’s finally out in the wild, players have had a swath of mixed opinions on the title; some are absolutely loving it and finding it a decent challenge, while others are disappointed by its combat, perceived lack of difficulty, and impossible-to-fail QTEs.
This last complaint has reared its head specifically around a sequence where players are meant to chase down enemies on a motorcycle, dodging and weaving through traffic on a winding highway in the mountains. Logan is desperately trying to rescue a group of captured mutants who’ve been shoved onto a truck, and the situation is dire — but some players have discovered that he’ll successfully catch up to the bad guys regardless of whether or not you actually pilot him in the right direction.
One of the most viral examples of this came from an X user named Clint Beastwood, who claimed to have put down his controller to see what would happen to Logan if he didn’t interfere. The result was Logan bouncing off of guard rails like a high-stakes game of pinball, somehow making his way through the sequence without dying.
However, it is possible for him to die after getting hit by on coming vehicles, though he’s paradoxically more likely to meet an untimely end if players actually take hold of the controller and try to help him avoid ending up like a bug on someone’s windshield.
He CAN die. You do not need to control the bike. https://t.co/76EI4lDAy8 pic.twitter.com/6mPKHnxNne
The resulting conversation has been a heated one; players are at odds with each other, with some finding this a comparatively small issue in a sequence meant to get players from point A to point B, while others, like YouTuber ChicoFilo, are calling the lack of player agency “just ridiculous.”
“This here is a total disgrace,” Brazilian influencer Eloohzinha said. “It's [a] QTE that you don't even need to press, it's a bike that you don't need to ride.”
Isso aqui é esculacho total. É QTE que você nao precisa apertar, é moto que voce nao precisa pilotar. É pérola atras de perola. Realmente, o prego no caixão foi esse wolverine. Ultimo jogo bom do estudio foi Ratchet And Clank e ja era. pic.twitter.com/hRUFzxmNDe
Decided to play Wolverine on the HARDEST difficulty and honestly it's been fun but this is just ridiculous 😭 #Wolverine #Playstation pic.twitter.com/fnoqSKazV6
“If Wolverine gets hit while on the bike, he can die. So you do need to control the bike. It’s posts like this that hurt real conversations around games,” popular YouTuber Mightykeef argued. “...if you can die, then it’s not autopilot. You need to control the bike, or else you can die and start over again. This type of on-rails segment happens in hundreds of action games.”
“Keyword being ‘if,’ when ‘if’ shouldn’t exist,” another user hit back. “There’s plenty of videos already out there showing players getting through the entire sequence without dying, regardless of difficulty.”
Keyword being “ IF “ when “ IF “ shouldn’t exist. There’s plenty of videos already out there showing players getting through the entire sequence without dying. Regardless of difficulty.
For now, players will just have to pick up the game themselves to form their own opinions on it. We at IGN gave it a six out of 10, saying its “good character work props up flashy combat that wears thin over time.” (Personally, I’m enjoying the game so far, and haven’t been annoyed by scent trails or QTEs just yet. I also liked the Omega Red boss fight, which seems to have been tripping up quite a few players onine.)
We’ve got 17 Essential Tips and Tricks to help you get started in Marvel’s Wolverine, plus our recommendations for the 10 Best Adaptations, and a guide on How to Farm XP Quickly. Check out our full Marvel’s Wolverine Walkthrough for a step-by-step guide to every mission, and make sure you don’t miss a thing with our Collectibles guides, All Wolverine Suits and Claws Guide, and our thorough list of all the Easter Eggs and References we've found.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: A pirate known for cracking games that utilize the DRM software Denuvo is being hit with a lawsuit... but that isn't stopping them from continuing on.
item.description:
A pirate known for cracking games that utilize the DRM software Denuvo is being hit with a lawsuit... but that isn't stopping them from continuing on.
For years, PC games have attempted to shield themselves from piracy with a DRM software known as Denuvo. The software is meant to be difficult to crack, with the hope that it will protect the game from becoming available for free on piracy sites around the time of launch. It does its job to a degree, as it took about a month and a half for Resident Evil Requiem to be cracked... and it was achieved by a pirate known as voices38.
As spotted by GamesRadar, the pirate is now being sued by Denuvo, so long as the company can actually identify who they are. The company is working to unmask this anonymous pirate and there's likely hope that even if they aren't successful, the pressure of an investigation will maybe spook voices38 into disappearing. That's not the case, though. voices38 took to Reddit to issue a statement, telling fellow pirates that "all is fine" and "everything will continue as normal."
It's an interesting story, and one that only feels all the more relevant with the recent GTA 6 leaks, when a leaker obtained access to the build of the highly anticipated game and taunted Rockstar Games with various messages. Once the game was properly revealed, the leaker vanished, and as of a month later, there has been no word as to whether or not they've been caught. Whether they'll return to cause more chaos remains to be seen, but it is pretty evident that online hackers and lawbreakers are getting good at evading detection.
Whether voices38 can continue to crack these games and get away with it is up in the air, but they certainly think they can.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: If you have Tony Stark levels of money, you can now own one of the most iconic and important pieces of Iron Man art ever published.
item.description:
Heritage Auctions has revealed a new lineup of classic comic book artwork included in the upcoming Comic Art Signature Auction event, and there are truly some doozies. Among them is an iconic page from 1968's Iron Man #1, originally owned by none other than Marvel Studios founding chairman David Maisel.
The art in question is the opening splash page from that issue, making it the very first piece of art from the very first solo Iron Man comic. The art was created by penciller Gene Colan and inker Johnny Craig. Check it out below:
Unsurprisingly, owning a true piece of comic book history like this won't come cheap. The page is currently up for auction, with the price as of the time of publish already reaching a whopping $6,750.
“Gene created two things,” Maisel said in a press release. “He made the suit expressive and almost limber, and he was very cinematic in his art, and almost foreseeing the MCU at some point in time, almost 40 years later. The combination of it being the historic first page of the first issue, the big art of a Page 1 splash, the fun ‘What a way to start out in your own mag’ and Gene’s art was something I couldn’t say no to.”
There are several other historic pages featured in this auction event. One is artist Jerry Robinson's cover to 1942's Detective Comics #68. Not only is that issue the second appearance of Two-Face, the sheer fact that a piece of original art from the Golden Age has survived in such good shape is pretty notable. The same goes for Joe Shuster's cover to 1940's Action Comics #22.
Other noteworthy listings include several pages from Frank Miller's seminal Daredevil run from the 1980s and Jim Lee's cover to 1992's X-Men #6 (which is currently bidding at an eye-watering $135,000). Clearly, collecting original comic art is not a hobby for the frugal.
Would you like to bid on this Iron Man #1 page or any of the other art featured above? Let us know in the comments.
For more, learn how the Marvel Masterworks line is making a comeback this year, see our exclusive interview about the upcoming finale of Star Trek: The Last Starship, and brush up on the 15 best Wolverine comics.

item.title: Michael B. Jordan is currently working on more than one anime project, and even joked that he might leave Hollywood behind to focus on anime full-time.
item.description:
Michael B. Jordan is currently working on more than one anime project, and even joked that he might leave Hollywood behind to focus on anime full-time.
It’s no secret that Michael B. Jordan is a huge anime fan. He’s been open about his love for iconic series like Dragon Ball, Hunter x Hunter, and Naruto, as well as famous films like Studio Ghibli’s Princess Mononoke. In fact, the last fight in Creed 3 was inspired by anime-style brawls, with the actor saying he took direct influence from boxing series Hajime no Ippo and Megalo Box. (Side note: If you haven’t watched Ippo, do yourself a favor and pull it up on Netflix right now.)
Now that Sinners has had some time to breathe, Jordan is diving into the anime world to make his own creations in the space, and even joked that he might ditch the world of traditional filmmaking to pursue his passion full time.
Jordan chatted about the subject in a cover interview for the October 2026 issue of Vogue, where the outlet revealed that he has “some [anime] projects in early stages of development.”
“I might just quit it all and make anime the rest of my life,” he told Vogue, with reporter Kelefa Sanneh remarking that he was “only half-joking.”
IGN got the chance to chat with Jordan back in February 2023, where he gushed about the anime that shaped Creed 3’s visual flair and combat sequences.
"Without nerding out too much... You've seen so many fights throughout the Rocky and Creed franchise, and I really wanted to put my spin on it, you know? How to make these fights different, and you know, from Hajime no Ippo, to Megalo Box, to Naruto, to My Hero Academia, all of those different anime that I watched growing up, there's an inherent spirit to them in how they fight..." he told us at IGN Fan Fest.
"And their bonds and relationships and all that good stuff. But it's very similar to the brotherhood and bond that we have, and his relationship to his family as well. So I tried to key in on some of those key moments. And yeah, they're in there. They're in a lot of the fights. …I would say from the Dragon Ball Z universe, there's a punch... [in] me and Damian's fight, where there's a Dragon Ball Z punch that's in there."
While it’s as-yet unclear what Jordan’s anime projects will be, fans can look forward to his performance alongside Austin Butler in Miami Vice '85, a reboot of the iconic 80s TV series that’s set to release on August 6, 2027.
Jordan is also working on a Battlefield movie alongside Christopher McQuarrie, with the two stars reportedly shopping the adaptation around to different studios in hopes of bringing Electronic Arts’ popular military game series to the silver screen.

item.title: Breakout hit Wardogs is outpacing Arc Raiders and Helldivers 2 on Steam in terms of copies sold at launch, new data shows.
item.description:
Breakout hit Wardogs is outpacing Arc Raiders and Helldivers 2 on Steam in terms of copies sold at launch, new data shows.
Bulkhead’s tactical first-person shooter released in early access form on Steam on September 10 and hit a peak of 428,666 concurrent players soon after, becoming one of the most-played games on Valve’s platform. It sold 1 million copies on day one and 1.25 million by day two. Bulkhead announced 2 million sales after just five days.
According to Rhys Elliott of Alinea Analytics, Wardogs is now up to 2.2 million copies sold on Steam, which means it’s outpacing Arc Raiders (1.7 million) and Helldivers 2 (1 million) when launch aligned on Valve’s platform.
Not only that, with approximately $70 million in revenue generated so far, Wardogs has already made more money on Steam alone than Bungie’s Marathon has managed across PC and console so far, Elliott’s data suggests. “It’s another reminder that, when it comes to live-service games, community trumps budget and pedigree,” he said.
The question now is can Wardogs maintain its momentum with both Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 and GTA 6 around the corner. Both Arc Raiders and Helldivers 2 enjoyed huge interest months after release, and went on to sell many millions of copies. Wardogs still has a long way to go before matching both games longer term, but it’s worth remembering Wardogs is in early access, where it will remain for 1-2 years. A console version planned for 2028. “We are adamant that we do not want to be in Early Access for a long time,” its Steam page reads. Overnight, Bulkhead boss Joe Brammer said Season 2 will bring “lots of new content and changes” now Wardogs was entering the next phase of development.
“Wardogs‘ growth story is far from over,” Elliott continued. “It’s got some maintenance hills to climb and a strong roadmap to deliver on before it can dream of reaching the heights of, say, an Arc Raiders.
“But make no mistake: even if it never sold another copy, Wardogs is already a huge success. It’s a $40 shooter aimed at a slightly unfashionable audience that stuck to its guns and turned out bloody great.
“You can’t really replicate what Bulkhead pulled off here, but they knew exactly who the game was for, priced it fairly, built the community before launch (and actually talked to them), cut the PR nonsense, were authentic (to a fault at times), and made something cool.”
On that $40 price point, Elliott suggested Wardogs hit “the modern pricing sweet spot, sitting below the friction point of a $70 AAA release while capturing that chunky volume of players priced out of premium titles.”
User reviews are now ‘Very Positive’ after initial complaints around launch problems. That appears to be done and dusted now, with players getting on with the game and having fun. A number of gameplay clips showing Wardogs shenanigans have gone viral (players are even avoiding Wardogs’ Lonestar faction over a perception that they seemingly attract the worst players and lose the most games).

item.title: Call of Duty developer Treyarch has said it’s “ready to make something new” as it waves goodbye to two years of Black Ops games.
item.description:
Call of Duty developer Treyarch has said it’s “ready to make something new” as it waves goodbye to two years of Black Ops games.
Treyarch led development on two Black Ops games back-to-back: 2024’s Black Ops 6 and 2025’s Black Ops 7. With Season 6 hitting Black Ops 7 on September 17, the developer has signalled it’s moving on to its next Call of Duty game.
“This is a bittersweet goodbye, but I think over the last two years, we've learned a lot,” design director Kevin Drew said in a new dev talk video. “We've tried a lot of things in our current era. But we're ready to make something new and something that nobody's ever experienced before. In the meantime though, I will see you all playing in Season 6 on September 17th.”
What this means, exactly, is unclear. Could Treyarch be talking about making a new Call of Duty game not in the Black Ops subbrand? Is Treyarch’s next Call of Duty not Black Ops 8? That would be something of a surprise, given Black Ops’ popularity and brand power despite Black Ops 7’s high-profile commercial struggles. Perhaps Treyarch is talking about doing something brand new within the Black Ops universe. My feeling though, is that this is indeed a hint that Black Ops may be given some time to rest, and that Treyarch has something different up its sleeve.
Yale Miller, co-studio head, added: “It’s been amazing to look back at the last couple of years, setting new benchmarks with Black Ops 6, delivering the biggest Black Ops game ever with Black Ops 7, taking huge swings with Omnimovement, Endgame, all kinds of innovation. We are extremely proud and extremely excited for what we were able to deliver.
“So, it's been amazing to actually also have a dialogue with all of you through regular comms, also through these dev talks, and we've been along with you every step of the way while we're delivering new innovative content. You guys have been grinding out camos, unlocking new things, the progression systems, the feedback. A huge thank you to our partner Raven and all the other studios that helped us here at Treyarch bring all of you all those maps, all that content, all those zombies experiences. It's been amazing.
“Really excited as well for everything Infinity Ward has been working on. They are clearly setting new bars. There's so much more of that game for all of you to see. We've had the privilege of taking part in a ton of playtests as well. We'll see you all online in Season 6 and in MW4. Thank you so much. It has been a privilege.”
Infinity Ward’s Modern Warfare 4 comes out later this year, but Activision has yet to say what will follow. It has an army of studios working on Call of Duty, which may need a shot in the arm from, say, Sledgehammer or Warzone developer Raven in the coming years. The question for parent company Microsoft and new Xbox boss Asha Sharma will be, how does Call of Duty once again hit the heights of yesteryear?
Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

item.title: Resident Evil director Zach Cregger has revealed which actress he would cast as a live-action Lady Dimitrescu — and we think he's made the perfect choice.
item.description:
Resident Evil director Zach Cregger has revealed which actress he would cast as a live-action Lady Dimitrescu — and we think he's made the perfect choice.
To be clear, the iconic Lady D from 2021's Resident Evil Village does not appear in Cregger's upcoming Resident Evil movie, as it tells an original story. So, don't expect to see her or any other fan favorites up on the big screen. That said, Cregger is a self-confessed Resident Evil aficionado, and seems to clearly know who he'd cast if given the chance.
"Christina Hendricks," Cregger said, when asked his pick for Lady D while in conversation with Pedestrian.TV. "That feels about right to me. What do you think?" Well, speaking personally, that seems like a solid call.
The vampire-like Lady Dimitrscu stole the hearts of many Resident Evil fans back when Village launched, with many players attracted to her giant stature and femme fatale design. Countless pieces of fan art followed, some more erotic than others, and Capcom leant into her popularity by providing life-size cardboard cutouts of the character in video game stores.
Even though Lady D hasn't returned to the series (so far), she remains a firm favorite — and notably her costume could be unlocked in this year's Resident Evil Requiem, if you stumped up for the game's Deluxe Edition.
Could we see the character appear in a future Resident Evil film? While Cregger has taken flak from some fans for deciding to make an original take on the franchise, early buzz for the movie has been positive, and the box office projections look strong. Indeed, Cregger has already said he has ideas for potential sequels. Here's hoping Christina Hendricks is free.

item.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day has overtaken Star Wars: The Force Awakens to become the highest-grossing movie of all time in North America.
item.description:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day has overtaken Star Wars: The Force Awakens to become the highest-grossing movie of all time in North America.
Domestic box office for the Tom Holland sequel is now up to $936.773 million, according to Variety. That puts it just ahead of 2015’s The Force Awakens, which is sitting on $936 million at the North American box office.
Of course, The Force Awakens came out 11 years ago, so there’s inflation to consider here. But Sony and Marvel owner Disney won’t care; Spider-Man: Brand New Day has been an astonishing success, so much so that even movie executives were taken by surprise.
Earlier this month, Sony Pictures chief Tom Rothman said that Brand New Day’s popularity was down to the fact that it is, essentially, a movie about “a lonely guy.”
If you’re one of the few who hasn’t seen Brand New Day yet, it picks up years after the events of 2021’s No Way Home, and shows Peter Parker struggling to cope with the absence of his friends and loved ones following Doctor Strange’s memory wipe spell. A decent chunk of the first act of the movie is spent showing Parker’s inner turmoil and, yes, his extreme loneliness, which is fueled by the end of his relationship with Zendaya’s MJ.
This, Rothman insisted, is the key to Brand New Day’s appeal. Brand New Day is “not so much a superhero film, but a super-person film,” he said. “The reason that movie has resonated all around the world is because it’s about a lonely guy… It’s like yeah, it’s about friendship. It’s very human. It’s very emotional. It’s got plenty of whiz-bang, but that’s not what the secret is. The secret is it’s a relatable story that almost everybody has related to.”
The big box office question now is will Brand New Day go on to hit the billion dollar mark at the domestic box office? As Variety notes, after 47 days in theaters, perhaps it will need a re-release or two to get there.
Brand New Day’s global total is now $2.4 billion, which makes it the third-highest grossing movie of all time behind only Avatar and Avengers: Endgame. Neither movie is in trouble of being overtaken by Brand New Day (Endgame is on $2.7 billion, Avatar, which came out in 2009, is on $2.9 billion).
Last week, it was reported that the inevitable Spider-Man sequel already has its director, with Deadline saying Destin Daniel Cretton will return for Marvel and Sony's fifth Tom Holland-starring Spider-Man movie. Given how well Cretton’s Brand New Day has done, that’s not a huge surprise.
Will this December’s Avengers: Doomsday, which has yet to confirm the appearance of a Spider-Man from this or any other universe, outperform Brand New Day?

item.title: A baby girl now has "Cineworld" listed as her official place of birth, after popping out during a recent screening of Harry Potter.
item.description:
A baby girl now has "Cineworld" listed as her official place of birth, after popping out during a recent Harry Potter screening.
Elsie Lamb was born around 45 minutes into Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (that's Sorcerer's Stone if you're in the U.S.). And now, officially, her birthplace has been recorded as the Cineworld movie theater in Broughton, North Wales.
BBC News reports that Potter-mad mom Molly Connah, 32, was overdue to give birth and had attended an appointment just hours earlier for a sweep — a process meant to encourage the start of labor. What happened next, then, could probably have been predicted — even if it still might have seemed like magic.
"I can remember the scene I was watching when I walked out," Connah said. "It was when Hagrid and Harry are buying his stuff to go to Hogwarts. I thought, 'something doesn't feel right'.
"It was getting more and more intense, and I didn't want anything to go wrong," she continued. "At that point I think my body just went into shock and it was pure adrenalin."
Thankfully, Connah was assisted by her mom, as well as staff at the Cineworld and nearby Starbucks, who provided towels and sheets.
"I said to my mum, 'I feel like I need to push,'" Connah recalled. "She said, 'you can't'. I said, 'I can't, I need to. I've got to'. Two pushes and my daughter was out."
Within minutes, an emergency medic and also Elsie Lamb's father had both made it to the scene, and the family was then transferred to hospital before the film's credits rolled. All are now doing well, it's reported, and have visited the Cineworld again to thank staff for their help.
Cineworld, meanwhile, have given the family four free tickets to a future showing, as they missed the end of the movie.
Harry Potter recently returned to theaters in celebration of the first film's 25th anniversary, and so Warner Bros. could wring out one last bit of nostalgia for its movies before the franchise is rebooted via HBO's Harry Potter TV series that debuts this Christmas.
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: Multiple developers of the disastrous MindsEye have said they’ve been laid off, casting doubt over the future of its controversial developer, Build A Rocket Boy.
item.description:
Multiple developers of the disastrous MindsEye have said they’ve been laid off, casting doubt over the future of its controversial developer, Build A Rocket Boy.
Story-driven action adventure game MindsEye was initially designed to be a part of Everywhere, the ‘Roblox for adults’ creation platform led by former Grand Theft Auto design chief Leslie Benzies. BARB eventually switched to focus on MindsEye, with the company ballooning in size to over 500 staff at peak.
But MindsEye flopped hard when it came out in June 2025, with players calling it "broken," "buggy," and "the worst game of 2025." Soon after, BARB said it was “heartbroken” over the issues players had faced with the game, and promised to release a series of patches to fix the significant performance problems, glitches, and AI behavior bugs. Benzies told staff that the studio would bounce back and relaunch MindsEye, blaming its struggles on internal and external "saboteurs," among other things. CEO Mark Gerhard said the studio had been investigating what he called “criminal activity” that took place around the launch of the game.
In July last year, IGN reported that the Scottish studio had issued at-risk of redundancy emails to its then around 300-strong UK workforce. Subsequent rounds of layoffs followed, and this summer, fired staff protested outside the studio over an “all-expenses-paid playtest day.”
BARB attempted to relaunch MindsEye with what was called the “Blacklisted” update, but it failed to move the needle. Subsequent updates and a last-ditch 50% off Steam sale have similarly fallen on deaf ears. While console player numbers are unavailable, MindsEye had a 24-hour peak Steam concurrent player count of just 16.
The extent of the layoffs is unclear at this stage, with one source familiar with the studio telling IGN that the company may not be dissolved even if all staff are let go. Either way, there are now serious questions over the future of the studio and MindsEye itself. IGN has asked BARB for comment.
Benzies was a crucial member of the Grand Theft Auto development team at Rockstar, and is considered one of the key architects of its enormous success. He left in 2016 amid a legal row over unpaid royalties that was eventually settled out of court. With the GTA link in place, BARB attracted more than £233 million ($313 million) of investment by 2024. Hitman developer IO Interactive snapped up publishing rights.
BARB's latest financial statements, made up to September 30, 2025, reveal it had generated revenue of £4.6 million ($6.1 million), but had total operating costs of £52.1 million ($70 million). It declared a net loss of £36.2 million ($48.6 million) for the period.
In May, Strauss Zelnick, boss of Rockstar parent company Take-Two, issued what sounded like a nod to BARB’s struggles. "Making hits seems to get harder and harder and harder as entertainment industries mature," Zelnick said, speaking at the TD Cowen 54th Annual Technology, Media & Telecom Conference.
"The folks at Rockstar seem to be able to make these massive hits, and lots of other people have tried. Lots and lots, including former Rockstar employees. And so far, they haven't been able to do it."

item.title: Netflix has revealed its logo for Narnia: The Magician's Nephew, the upcoming fantasy blockbuster directed by Barbie's Greta Gerwig.
item.description:
Netflix has revealed its logo for Narnia: The Magician's Nephew, the upcoming fantasy blockbuster directed by Barbie's Greta Gerwig.
For almost three months, the Netflix-made Narnia will be exclusive to theaters from its release on February 12, with IMAX previews beginning on February 10. Netflix subscribers will then be able to stream the movie, but only from April 2 onwards.
While Netflix has given short theatrical windows to a few other films, this extended period is extremely unusual. Martin Scorsese's The Irishman was available via limited theatrical release for less than a month, while Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery had just a single week in theaters before it dropped onto Netflix.
The Magician's Nephew is chronologically the first book in C. S. Lewis' beloved Narnia series, though most adaptations to date have begun with The Lion, The Witch and The Wardrobe — the first Narnia story published, and by far the most famous. Indeed, The Magician's Nephew has never been adapted for the screen until now.
Clearly, though, Netflix hopes that this fresh entry point into the franchise will be a successful start to its plans for the series, with an all-star cast and years of work to bring the story to life. Carey Mulligan, Daniel Craig, Emma Mackey, Ciarán Hinds and Meryl Streep all feature in the film, with its young leads played by newcomers David McKenna and Beatrice Campbell.
Don't expect Netflix to make theatrical releases the norm for its movies in future, however. Netflix film boss Dan Lin recently said that the streamer "just won't work with" filmmakers who push to bring their films to the big screen — with Gerwig seemingly a notable exception.

item.title: Pokémon's coveted 30th anniversary trading card set has gone on sale, though its launch has seen some stores jacking up prices, while long lines of customers have camped outside overnight.
item.description:
Pokémon's coveted 30th anniversary trading card set has gone on sale, though its launch has seen some stores jacking up prices, while long lines of customers have camped outside overnight.
High demand and a limited supply have impacted every recent Pokémon card release, but huge attention is being paid to this launch in particular due to its nostalgic re-release of beloved cards, as well as some ultra rare new designs.
Of course, much of this demand is driven by the lucrative resale market, with a quick profit to be made online when flogging unopened boxes or rare individual cards. Some retailers have started to limit individual purchase amounts, or even cut open packaging to destroy cards' resale value. In Japan, facial recognition has even been introduced at some stores. But none of this seems to have stemmed demand, as shoppers have descended on retailers in the hopes of snagging whatever stock they have.
Retailers taking advantage of this include GameStop, which is selling the $49.99 Elite Trainer Box of cards for $169.99, a stunt it has pulled previously. Dick's Sporting Goods, meanwhile, has the same package for a slightly cheaper $119.99 (thanks, Polygon) — still more than double the upfront cost).
Long queues have been spotted this morning in both the U.K. and France, where the cards are now on sale. Numerous fans pitched up tents or slept on camping chairs to keep their spot in the queue:
A huge queue outside The Entertainer in Altrincham this morning as Pokémon fans wait to get their hands on a special release of trading cards marking the game’s 30th birthday.The gentleman in the grey hoodie at the front of the queue had been waiting since 10pm last night -… pic.twitter.com/7R76wsJflF
Depuis 18h40 devant le mag pour les Pokemon 30 ans pic.twitter.com/lZWjGOiXCp
🤣🤣🤣🤣🤣🤣🤣 des gens ont dormis dehors toute une nuit pour être les premiers à avoir des cartes pour les 30 ans de Pokemon 🤣🤣🤣🤣🤣🤣🤣🤣 mais reste chez eux quand y’a des manifs pour le prix de l’essence etc etc 🫪 pic.twitter.com/ATvBV6Ybwq
Énorme file d'attente au Cultura de La Defense pour acheter les cartes Pokémon 30 ans.Les premiers clients ont passé la nuit devant le magasin. pic.twitter.com/oe9kwcOcJd
Colchester Smyths is currently full of people, even camping in the road! This is absurd!!!!!!!!!!! 🤯🤯 @PokemonStockUK pic.twitter.com/xcA3nzgvDQ
On the other side of the Atlantic, lines of fans outside stores began several days ago in some locations. There has also been criticism of people reserving their spot with so-called 'ghost chairs' — essentially leaving a seat in place to mark a spot, days in advance.
The idea here is that you are forming a line of chairs that are then left empty, days before the thing you are actually lining up for. On the one hand, it's a practice that will save a lot of people from several uncomfortable days parked out on the street. On the other, it hardly seems fair to those who do turn up on the day of release to a row of empty seats in front of them.
What happens if you turn up to queue — potentially overnight — and there are already chairs in front? Being there in person, do you get priority over a 'ghost chair' spot reserved by someone who is not? It is situations like these that are likely to prompt the squabbles that often break out during such gatherings ahead of product launches, especially if you've been left grumpy by a night in the cold.
The lines for Pokemon 30th Celebration have started and they're WILD🎥: IG/pokegirlbecca pic.twitter.com/ad6zmD59jY
Pokémon 30th Anniversary x Best Buy More ghost chairs, Best Buy just doesn't care at this point https://t.co/BtaiXmNids pic.twitter.com/m1eXOxRS1A
Pokémon cards have become a prime target for scalpers and thieves over the past few years due to their soaring popularity and the perceived value of rare cards. New card releases frequently sell out completely, and The Pokémon Company has appeared unable or unwilling to fully keep up with demand — despite a staggering 10 billion cards printed last year alone.
Earlier this week, one millionaire Pokémon collector suggested that the cards will likely be used as currency following a global apocalypse. Looking to start your collection? We've also got a list of the 10 most expensive Pokémon cards of 2026 so far, and a first look at Mega Evolution's Delta Reign expansion, set to release in November this year.
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: Development images for a Tiny Tina’s Wonderlands sequel and a new Brothers in Arms game have emerged online, amid reports both were scrapped.
item.description:
Development images for a Tiny Tina’s Wonderlands sequel and a new Brothers in Arms game have emerged online, amid reports both were scrapped.
MP1st, which published the work-in-progress images, said the games were in development at former Embracer-owned studio Lost Boys Interactive, which returned to independence last year. Embracer sold Gearbox to 2K Games parent company Take-Two in 2024.
Lost Boys Interactive worked on the original Tiny Tina’s Wonderlands, a fantasy-themed spinoff of Gearbox’s hugely successful Borderlands franchise, as well as Borderlands 4, so it’s not a huge surprise to see evidence that it worked on the sequel.
Indeed, it was thought that Tiny Tina’s Wonderlands did so well commercially that a sequel was inevitable. In 2022, Gearbox chief Randy Pitchford called Tiny Tina’s Wonderlands a “major victory,” adding that the developer viewed it as a new franchise with “future experiences already under development.”
“Wonderlands shattered all of our target expectations, both critically and commercially,” said Pitchford during an Embracer Group annual general meeting, “and I'm thrilled to report that in addition to great financial rewards from this victory that will be coming our way in the coming quarters, we have established a firm beachhead, and we now clearly have a new franchise on our hands.”
However, since then, nothing has emerged on a new Tiny Tina’s Wonderlands game. Gearbox has yet to announce its next project following last year’s release of Borderlands 4.
Meanwhile, the last mainline Brothers in Arms game was 2008’s Brothers in Arms: Hell's Highway. A fourth game in the WW2 shooter series, Furious 4, was cancelled and eventually turned into ill-fated hero shooter Battleborn. Pitchford has over the years indicated that a new Brothers in Arms game was on the way, but it never materialised.
The released images don’t really tell us much about the games themselves, other than they were in development. Were they canceled as part of Gearbox's sale to Take-Two? Are there new versions of each game in the works somewhere at Gearbox? IGN has asked for comment.
Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

item.title: Microsoft has insisted it's yet to "finalize" any changes to Xbox Game Pass, after a potential leak detailed plans to drop the inclusion of new titles from day one.
item.description:
Microsoft has insisted it's yet to "finalize" any changes to Xbox Game Pass, after a potential leak detailed plans to drop the inclusion of new titles from day one.
Since the introduction of Game Pass, Xbox has repeatedly changed how day one game releases are included in the subscription — from the introduction of a more expensive Ultimate tier (and various pricing changes up and down for that), plus Call of Duty's exclusion last fall.
This week, word began to spread online that day one games would be ditched from Game Pass altogether as soon as next spring, as part of upcoming moves that seem designed to improve margins, while also offering the subscription at a slightly lower and more attractive price point.
The changes were first discussed by Slayven, a moderator on video game forum ResetEra who stated previously shared accurate plans of other past Game Pass changes.
According to Slayven, Microsoft will offer two Xbox Game Pass subscriptions going forward — with and without advertising. The former will cost $12.99 a month, while the latter will cost $19.99 or $239.99 annually.
For the option without ads, this results in a small $3/month saving — though with the caveat that day one games will no longer be available. Cloud streaming and a family plan option will now be separate bolt-on costs ($5.99/month each).
There's word of online multiplayer also being available as a separate charge, though the details here are a little unclear. In what sounds like a new form of the Xbox Game Pass Essential experience, you'll be able to pay just for online gameplay, or with access to a game library.
In response to these details hitting the internet, Forbes reporter Paul Tassi received a statement from a Microsoft spokesperson that notably did not discount the leak as incorrect. Instead, the statement merely suggests that final decisions on any change have not yet been made, and there is nothing concrete to confirm right now. Here's that statement in full:
"We regularly test different Game Pass offerings and look at what works best for players in different markets. We don't have any changes to announce today or plans that have been finalized. There are no changes to previously announced games coming to Game Pass Ultimate on day one."
Xbox boss Asha Sharma has previously discussed the potential for including advertising as a way to lower the price of services such as Game Pass, so its introduction next year is not too much of a surprise. There has also long been a sense that Microsoft has struggled to balance the books with its offer of day one games — as seen in the sky-high price that Game Pass Ultimate previously reached, as well as the subsequent decision to exclude Call of Duty instead.
Removing day one games from Game Pass would presumably make the service less of a loss leader, while encouraging far more Xbox owners to splash out on the games Microsoft has ploughed millions into making. But it would also be a huge loss to attraction of Game Pass, that would inevitably lead some fans to unsubscribe.
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: The development team behind Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave has discussed the choice to provide just one save file — and why it shouldn't matter.
item.description:
The development team behind Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave has discussed the choice to provide just one save file — and why it shouldn't matter.
Nintendo and Intelligent System's promising-looking strategy RPG features four swappable protagonists during its first half, plus numerous ways to customize each character and recruit an array of followers. But the game has been designed in a way that rewards the player if they do replay certain sections, and no content is permanently missable.
Indeed, the idea that players' experiences can converge into one overall progression path mirrors the game's own structure, which switches to a single hero for its latter half, aided by the four protagonists that players have already come to know and (hopefully) love.
"The idea of things converging into one is a core concept behind the story, and in terms of gameplay, we believe that everything players experience in the game has value," director Toshiyuki Kusakihara said, as part of an Ask the Developer interview. "The basic idea was to create a system where nothing players go through is ever wasted. Everything is preserved and eventually coalesces into a whole. In Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, players can progress through multiple paths simultaneously as well as replay the same path multiple times. To ensure that none of the experiences players had accumulated would go to waste, we felt that consolidating everything into a single save file was the best approach for this game."
"Of course, I’m sure there are players who prefer to keep multiple save files, and I'm actually one of those players myself," associate producer Kenta Nakanishi said. "But because the game system of Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave is built around multiple paths, having separate save files would create system-related complications. It becomes difficult to keep track of how far players have progressed in each protagonist's story when that progress is spread across multiple save files. So rather than simply limiting the game to a single save file, we added other creative ideas to make the system work better.
"In this game, we preserved save data from the start of every chapter for each main protagonist, and made it possible for players to jump back to those points," Nakanishi continued. "If players think, 'I want to play this chapter again', they can play again from the beginning of the selected chapter. This feature isn't just for replaying chapters, either. Players can use it to review maps, revisit specific cutscenes, or even retry particular battles, so we hope players will make full use of it."
"On top of that, players can repeatedly go back into the past using the Goddess of Fate's power and retry situations as many times as they like," Kusakihara concluded. "In that sense, I think the game's system ties in very closely with the story, as both revolve around the concept of retrying, building upon past experiences, and ultimately weaving those experiences together into a single outcome."
While telling a standalone story, Fortune's Weave is a clear successor to the Switch's hugely-popular Fire Emblem: Three Houses, with many of the same development team returning, and the game itself featuring familiar elements and at least one returning character. For this follow-up, its developers were keen to expand Three Houses' trio of teams, and initially wanted a whopping eight characters to follow. This was then ultimately halved to four, with Eshmel later added as a fifth, to tie the game's opening quartet together.
"Kusakihara-san had really developed a clear theme for each protagonist, and I felt it could lead to something really interesting," producer Genki Yokota said. "But with eight protagonists, there was almost too much we could do... It seemed like players would have a lot to keep track of, which could make the game feel complicated. So we decided to put the focus on four of those protagonists instead."
"Eshmel plays a slightly different role from the four protagonists," Kusakihara added. "The game begins with the player controlling Eshmel, but to be honest, this character didn't even exist until partway through development. Eshmel was another protagonist we added right at the end. Our initial idea was that players would choose whichever of the four protagonists they liked and then keep fighting with that protagonist through to the end. But something about that never quite felt right to me. The issue was that it didn't really feel like the four stories were coming together into one in a satisfying way.
"As I mentioned earlier, once the game reaches its second half, the story comes together into one, and the four protagonists gather in one place. But even after that, if we continued to follow the story through each of their individual perspectives, it just wouldn't have felt like it matched the concept of multiple stories converging into one. That led us to realise that we needed another character who could take a broader view of all four protagonists. So our thinking was, 'If we just had one more person, all the stories would come together nicely!' And that's how Eshmel was born. We were already halfway through development, but I went to the team and said, 'Sorry, but we’re adding one more character'. (Laughs)"
Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave launches tomorrow, September 17, exclusively for Nintendo Switch 2.
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: Sony has released a fresh system software update for the PS5 that makes a number of interesting changes. Check out the version 26.06-14.00.00 patch notes.
item.description:
Sony has released a fresh system software update for the PlayStation 5 that makes a number of interesting changes.
Version 26.06-14.00.00 turns on Enhance PSSR Image Quality as a default setting. The PS5 Pro-exclusive feature is used even for games that support the previous version of PSSR, “so you can enjoy a sharper and clearer visual experience,” Sony said in a post on its website. You can turn it off if you want.
Elsewhere, you can now see who’s speaking while you’re in a voice chat by turning on Display Names, (details on how to enable this are in the patch notes, below). You can even choose where the speaker indicator appears on your screen.
Here’s an interesting one: the update lets you see Trending Now and Top 10 via the Community Activity widget in your Welcome Hub. Trending Now displays 10 multiplayer games or modes that are “surging in popularity,” Sony said. It sounds like the intention here is to surface new game releases or games with big updates.
Top 10, meanwhile, displays the 10 most popular games in the last week for your country or region. This isn’t information Sony usually provides publicly, so it will be interesting to see what ends up on the list. We don’t know how the list is determined, however. Is it total number of players during the period? Is it by peak concurrents? Play time? “Look here to see what games have a large community of players you can join,” Sony said.
And, not wanting to be left out, the PS4 also has a system software update today, although don’t expect revelations from the patch notes. Version 14.00 improves “system software performance and stability.” Sony, you really do spoil us with these patch notes.
The PS5 update arrives alongside the release of the latest big exclusive from Sony: Marvel’s Wolverine. item.description:
Wo Long 2: Wings of Ember, the upcoming action-soulslike sequel from Team Ninja (Nier, Ninja Gaiden), will be released on March 4, 2027 for PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S (including day one on Xbox Game Pass Ultimate), and Nintendo Switch 2. Meanwhile, a free playable alpha demo is available now on PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC. The demo will only be active for a limited time, from now through September 30.
Team Ninja says that the demo includes an in-progress character creator to try out as well as online multiplayer for up to three players. "Fans can explore the open field of Changban, join forces with Liu Bei’s army in fierce battles against the pursuing forces of Cao Cao, and encounter demons inspired by legendary Chinese classics," the developer said. In addition, anyone who plays and completes the demo will unlock the Fledgling Phoenix Helmet cosmetic item for use in the full game.
The original Wo Long was released in early 2023 and our resident soulslike superfan Mitchell Saltzman thought it was great, saying, "When it comes to the clashing of melee weapons, Wo Long is among the best in the genre, full stop." We also had it at #6 in our list of top-10 soulslikes published later in 2023.
Wo Long 2 was announced at this year's Xbox Showcase.
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

item.title: Joe Brammer, the CEO of Wardogs developer Bulkhead, has stated that the studio avoids hiring people that aren't willing to crunch.
item.description:
Joe Brammer, the CEO of Wardogs developer Bulkhead, has stated that the studio avoids hiring people who aren't willing to crunch.
In an interview with The Game Business, Brammer was asked about the studio's approach to crunch. He noted that he values balance, but not in the way people may think. Instead of traditional work weeks, the team will push harder for a handful of months, but then have the opportunity to take their foot off the gas without fear of retaliation.
"For the last three months, Wardogs has been a lot more important than a lot of their family lives," said Brammer. "It has been, because that's what pays the money for them. But now Bulkhead has to acknowledge that it needs to go the other way. For example, everyone is pushing us to get console out earlier.
"We've just said, 'No, you don't understand, that's not how it's going to work. We can't push them more. We're not doing that. It's going to release in 2028 when we say it's going to release.' So, for me it's about balance and helping people and making sure they have a company where they can say, 'I'm tapping out,' and not feel like they're going to get fired for tapping out."
Brammer went on to note that it has become harder to crunch due to the team getting older and trying to start families. He stated that they initially offered 10-week paternity leave, but eventually had to ditch it because the employees' partners were struggling to handle them going back to work. Instead, Bulkhead now offers 2-weeks of paternity leave and gives half-days to employees as a way of making the transition easier for the families.
Brammer also stated that they don't hire people who actively speak out against crunch in the industry on social media, as he believes they won't be a good fit for Bulkhead.
"A lot of people who may have an issue with crunch — rightly so, I understand that issue, we always try and avoid it, but we don’t hide that this is going to happen at some point — they often don't make it in the door," he says. "We want to be known for that: this is a place you come to work hard. If you care about the work you’re making and the result of what you make here, you'll feel really valued. If you don't, you will feel slave-driven."
Brammer's belief that the team must crunch has prompted Bulkhead to create incentives for developers. The team dishes out a "meaningful amount" in bonuses and shares in the company to select employees, though not everyone is eligible.
"If we're going to be a company who says, 'we do crunch', then we have to also say, 'but you get something for it,'" he said. "We want people to know that those people who do work hard get that return, and it is life-changing."
Wardogs has already sold a whopping 2 million copies in less than a week, meaning those incentivized employees are probably (hopefully) being justly compensated. The game is sitting near the top of Steam's most played games chart and is continuing to grow as word of mouth spreads. As noted by Brammer, Wardogs is also coming to consoles in 2028, and the team is going to take its sweet time getting there.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Marvel's Wolverine explains why Logan's clothes can heal, just like his body.
item.description:
Marvel's Wolverine explains why Logan's clothes can heal, just like his body.
Near the beginning of Marvel's Wolverine, Logan is gifted a proper superhero suit from Walter Langkowski. It's Wolverine's signature suit from the comics, cowl and all. Langkowski explains that his suit utilizes nano-tech, which can autorepair Logan's suit in the field. It's a clever workaround to make sure Wolverine's suit doesn't get shredded to the point of no return, leaving him to run around in the nude (though, that's not really out of character, either).
However, this isn't just any ordinary nano-tech: it's Phalanx. In Marvel lore, Phalanx are a cybernetic species that go up against the X-Men and other heroes. They use their techno-organic lifeforms to infect other species and create a hivemind. Whether this has any larger implications remains to be seen, but it's likely more of a fun way to explain things to fans using established material from the Marvel universe. In the MCU, nano-tech is extremely popular and is used prominently by Iron Man, Spider-Man, Black Panther, and the entire Avengers team in Endgame. It's nifty, though some feel like the films have begun to over-rely on it for suits.
In X-Men Origins: Wolverine, a game that Insomniac's new title takes a lot of inspiration from, Logan's wounds would also heal when out of combat. This sometimes meant that his clothes would re-generate too, but there wasn't really an in-universe reason for this, though no one seemed to care back then.

item.title: The CEO of HBO says he “thinks” The Last of Us showrunner Craig Mazin has planned for the series to end on a third and final season.
item.description:
The CEO of HBO says he “thinks” The Last of Us showrunner Craig Mazin has planned for the series to end on a third and final season.
HBO’s adaptation of Naughty Dog’s critically-acclaimed game franchise is coming to an end. At least, that’s what the Chairman and CEO of HBO and Max Content, Casey Bloys, all but admitted to Deadline during the streamer’s Emmys afterparty on Monday.
Speaking with the outlet, Bloys stated that The Last of Us Season 3 will take place in 2027, though he didn’t have a specific date to share. He also wouldn’t directly confirm whether or not it would be the show’s last season, but said he “thinks” it’s been planned as the end of the series.
“I think [showrunner] Craig [Mazin] has planned it as the final season,” he told Deadline.
This isn’t a huge surprise; Bloys has been indicating as much for the last year, telling Deadline in January when asked if Season 3 will be the show’s last that “it certainly seems that way, but on decisions like that, we will defer to the showrunners. So you can ask them.”
However, in May 2025, Craig Mazin was singing a decidedly different tune, saying a fourth season was necessary to wrap everything up.
“There’s no way to complete this narrative in a third season,” he told Collider at the time. "Hopefully, we’ll earn our keep enough to come back and finish it in a fourth. That’s the most likely outcome."
Season 3 of TLOU was announced before Season 2 had ever started. The show’s first season was met with critical acclaim, with IGN’s Simon Cardy scoring the show a nine out of 10. Its second season, however, stumbled, with many viewers taking issue with Bella Ramsey’s portrayal of Ellie in the adult stage of her life. IGN scored Season 2 a seven out of 10, with Cardy saying it was “still good, but it’s also a sequel that struggles because it’s only half of the story.”
While it’s looking more likely than ever that the show might be coming to an end next year, Naughty Dog has made it clear that it isn’t done with its flagship zombie franchise, even though it stepped back in its involvement with HBO’s screen adaptation for its third season.
"It's important for us to note that as the creator of the games, Naughty Dog is still the steward of this IP and even though this might be the end of this adaptation," Naughty Dog boss Neil Druckmann said to the Washington Post earlier this month. “We're not done with The Last of Us. There's a couple projects in the works that, when the time is right, I'm very excited to talk about."
For now, the studio is focused on its next offering, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, which recently finished filming its performance capture in August — though its lack of an appearance at the September 2026 State of Play left some fans disappointed.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.
